title: Students are the future of the largest democracy in the world: CEC Gyanesh Kumar
body_text:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) organised the second regional conference on “Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC 2.0) and ECINET” in Lucknow today. The conference focuses on strengthening electoral literacy and democratic awareness among young citizens through educational institutions. Addressing the participants comprising students and teachers from schools and colleges across Uttar Pradesh, describing students as the future of the nation, CEC Gyanesh Kumar said the ELCs are imperative to carry forth the knowledge and the understanding of electoral processes and enrich democracy. CEC Gyanesh Kumar stated how elections in India are held strictly as per the constitution of India, law and instructions issued by ECI and is conducted transparently under the concurrent audit of political parties, candidates or their representatives at all stages. He underlined the need for students and young electors to familiarise students and young electors with India’s electoral system, democratic values, electoral registration, polling and counting processes, and the role and functioning of the Election Commission of India. Emphasising the importance of engaging young citizens, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar stated that their trust and informed participation in the electoral process is an investment in the future of democracy. ELC 2.0, with the tagline, “Learn Democracy. Lead Democracy.”, reinforces the objective of encouraging young and first-time voters not only to understand democracy but also to participate meaningfully and contribute to its progress. Earlier in the day Shri Gyanesh Kumar visited his alma mater, Colvin Taluqdar’s College and interacted with the teachers and students at the school. Tomorrow, the second day of the visit, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar will hold an interaction with Booth Level Officers (BLOs) of Uttar Pradesh. ELC 2.0 reimagines Electoral Literacy Clubs as structured, visible and digitally enabled platforms across schools, colleges and universities. The initiative envisages continuous, year-round activities to promote electoral literacy among young citizens and electoral awareness within their families, educational institutions and communities. ELC 2.0 will leverage the extensive ECINet digital platform which provides all election related services from roll to poll at the click of a button. A streamlined pan-India network of ELCs will be cultivated using a dedicated ELC portal on ECINet. The initiative assumes significance in view of India’s extensive educational ecosystem, comprising approximately 15 lakh schools with nearly 25 crore students and over one crore teachers. The higher education sector comprises nearly 1,500 universities and around 70,000 educational institutions, with an estimated enrolment of 4.33 crore students. Through this extensive institutional network, ELC 2.0 seeks to promote factual and experiential electoral education, enhance awareness about the transparency, integrity and credibility of India’s electoral system, and encourage young citizens to become ambassadors of informed democratic participation. The ELCs will also serve as platforms for disseminating information about different stages of the electoral process, including electoral registration, polling and counting, along with the ECINET App and other key initiatives of the Election Commission of India.
*****
PK/GDH/RP

enrichment.summary: The Election Commission of India held its second regional conference on "Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC 2.0) and ECINET" in Lucknow, addressing students and teachers from schools and colleges across Uttar Pradesh. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar emphasised that students are the future of democracy and highlighted ELC 2.0's tagline "Learn Democracy. Lead Democracy." as a digitally-enabled initiative leveraging the ECINET platform to spread electoral literacy across India's vast educational network of roughly 15 lakh schools and 1,500 universities.
enrichment.context:
Electoral Literacy Clubs were first introduced by the ECI to build democratic awareness among young and future voters, particularly first-time voters who are often under-registered. ELC 2.0 represents a relaunch/upgrade of this initiative, integrating it with ECINET, the ECI's unified digital platform that consolidates services from voter roll management to counting ("roll to poll"). This reflects a broader ECI push toward digitisation of electoral administration and outreach, following other tech-enabled reforms like the Voter Helpline app and online enrollment services.

The initiative is significant given India's demographic profile, where a large share of eligible voters are young and first-time electors; low youth registration and turnout have historically been a concern for the ECI. By embedding electoral literacy within the school and college ecosystem, the ECI aims to institutionalise civic education and build long-term trust in electoral processes, especially amid periodic public debates about the integrity and transparency of elections.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary objective of the Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC) initiative of the Election Commission of India?
options: To provide financial subsidies to political parties
To promote electoral awareness and democratic participation among students
To regulate campaign finance in elections
prelims_questions.explanation: ELCs are platforms in schools and colleges designed to familiarise students with India's electoral system, registration, polling, and counting processes, encouraging informed democratic participation.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of electoral literacy initiatives like the Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC) in strengthening democratic participation among young and first-time voters in India.
